articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Beta Will Be Playable on Switch 2 for Free This Weekend
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend. Starting Friday, August 28 at 10 AM PDT, Nintendo Switch 2 players will have the opportunity to try Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for free.
body: The Switch 2 version will boast unique features such as gyro controls, Joy-Con mouse controls, and, of course, being able to play the game on a handheld. Additionally, Switch 2 players will get free access to the game's Vault Edition content during the beta. This includes access to special skins, weapon blueprints, and more. Players can pre-load the beta on Switch 2 right now and pre-order the full game.

It's the first time a Call of Duty game has been on a Nintendo platform since Call of Duty: Ghosts on Wii U. Nintendo fans have been wanting to see the franchise return to Nintendo hardware since then, but it hasn't been feasible until now. Digital Legends are developing the game's Switch 2 version after having helped develop Call of Duty: Warzone Mobile before its cancelation. The studio also did support work on the last two Black Ops games.
points: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend.

articles.title: 6 indie.io Games Coming to gamescom and PAX West That Have Free Demos on Steam
articles.summary: Publishing platform indie.io will be on hand at gamescom and PAX West in the coming weeks, and it’s bringing six games for people to try out in person. But if you’re not one of the lucky people who can be there yourself, don’t worry: all six games have free demos you can play on Steam right now, no…
body: As tends to be the case with indie.io, their selection of games covers a wide range of genres. There’s everything from a cozy vineyard château builder to a brutal turn-based roguelite RPG. There’s a little something for all kinds of gamers, and you can try out all of them right now.

If you watched IGN’s recent Indie Loop showcase, you would have seen this game under another name. Formerly called Monster Zoo Tycoon, it unveiled its new name on August 10, but the dev team and core gameplay remain the same. In Monster Park Tycoon from developer OverPowered Team, you build and manage a monster park where visitors can come see a variety of strange and terrifying abominations. But there’s a twist: your park is a front for a cult. Not a very smart cult, at that.

In order to expand your park, you’ll need to trick and capture your guests using traps disguised as park props. Once you’ve got them, you can either feed them to your monsters, brainwash them to turn them into cultists, or sacrifice them to gain Faith and unlock favors from your Dark Lord.

articles.title: Elden Ring On Switch 2 Is A Compromise, But It’s A Surprisingly Good One
articles.summary: Elden Ring was in rough shape on Switch 2 when people first tried it out last year, leading publisher Bandai Namco to significantly delay its launch plans. It's now 2026, and ahead of its new release date of August 28, has that extra time in the development oven helped smooth out Elden Ring on the…
body: Senior video producer Jake Dekker has spent over a week with the game, playing it in both docked and handheld modes. The key takeaway is that Elden Ring runs at a consistent frame rate, but not the highest one.

"While there are certainly frame rate drops, it never hits the lows that we saw in some of that preview footage," Dekker explained. It runs a lot better. That being said, the frame rate is still far from perfect. I've done most of my playing docked, but I've also done some handheld, and you definitely notice those frame rate drops here and there. I don't think it's so bad that it's distracting or unplayable. But for those who played Elden Ring on PC, Xbox Series X, or PlayStation 5, you're definitely going to notice the frame rate. It's not hitting that smooth 60 frames per second that we saw in those versions. And to be honest, that is a little disappointing."

articles.title: I've Tried Star Wars Zero Company on Five Different PCs, and It's Been a Nightmare
articles.summary: We got off to such a great start this year, with a ton of PC games that looked great and still ran well on pretty much any hardware. One of the common themes among games like Crimson Desert, Resident Evil Requiem, and Forza Horizon 6 was that none of them were running on Unreal Engine 5.
body: I've spent about five hours in Zero Company so far, and while that means I'm still pretty early in the otherwise fantastic game, I've still run into more than my fair share of technical issues, across all types of hardware. When the game isn't bugging out in some way, I've been having a blast with it, and it's important to note that our reviewer Dan Stapleton hasn't had nearly the same depth of issues that I've had.
What's funny is that the technical problems are different on each of the systems I've tried the game on.

I was on vacation last week, so the first laptop I tried the game on was my Razer Blade 16, with an RTX 5090 and a Ryzen AI 9 HX 370. It got a decent average frame rate at 1600p, but it was plagued with microstutters, especially in cutscenes. I started getting driver crashes, where the game would just make my laptop restart whenever I tried to load the game up — something that doesn't happen with any other game right now.

articles.title: Leaker Posts Extended Gameplay From GTA 6 Prologue Just Hours After Rockstar Warns Fans to Expect Story Spoilers
articles.summary: Extended gameplay footage revealing Grand Theft Auto 6's story prologue has been posted online, in a significant escalation of the past week's continued leaks. More than four minutes of gameplay featuring GTA 6 character Lucia is now being spread over social media, in the first lengthy leak of…
body: The footage's release comes just hours after Rockstar finally broke its silence over the leaks, which it called "heartbreaking" for its development team. In its statement, published online earlier today, the developer warned fans that spoilers would likely impact the manner in which it had hoped players would first experience the game — something that now appears to accurate.

A fresh statement from the leaker, included as a watermark in this latest footage, makes several unsubtantiated claims about GTA 6's development, such as the game still being unfinished and that there was "too much" work left on the game to comfortably complete it before the title's November 19 release date.

Earlier today, Rockstar noted that it was indeed still working on the game — something that is fully to be expected with nearly three months left to go until launch — but that it was now "nearly" finished. The company also reiterated GTA 6's November 19 launch date, suggesting confidence that nothing would change.

articles.summary: Microsoft has announced that preorders for the 25th-anniversary edition of the Xbox Series X are now open (at least to some), and if you want one, it's going to cost you. As rumored, the 1TB console will cost $900, which is $100 more than the standard Xbox Series X.
body: Additionally, Microsoft has announced that all of the 25th anniversary Xbox consoles will include a download code for Halo: Campaign Evolved.

The game launched in July, and while Halo's co-creator had some issues with it, he and others, including us here at GameSpot, generally enjoyed the remake. It's also the first Halo game on PlayStation.

articles.title: PlayStation Plus Free Games For September 2026 Revealed
articles.summary: PlayStation has revealed this month's batch of free games for PlayStation Plus subscribers. All PS Plus members will be able to claim four freebies starting September 1-- Sniper Elite: Resistance, MLB The Show 26, Chained Echoes, and Wobbly Life.
body: Sniper Elite: Resistance is the main event for September, and if you haven't checked out this series yet, then you've missed out on a gruesomely fun World War II adventure. Set behind enemy lines in occupied France, players will get to take on the Axis forces, one bullet at a time. Like the previous games, kills are highlighted in all their gory detail, and when you don't feel like taking out enemies from a long distance, there are plenty of options you can utilize to remove Nazis up close.

For something completely different, you can also aim for baseball glory in MLB The Show 26. This year's entry in the annual series plays to its strengths, offering authentic gameplay, evolved features, new stadium effects, and more as you play through various leagues from across multiple eras of baseball. If you're in the mood for a game that involves friends, you can check out Wobbly Life for some co-op chaos, as your gang explores an open-world sandbox full of diversions. You can also play it solo, but what's the fun in that?

articles.title: Video Game Icon Tim Curry Dies at 80
articles.summary: Tim Curry, the beloved English actor who played iconic and eccentric roles like the scientist Dr. Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Picture Show, the harried butler Wadsworth in Clue, and Pennywise the Clown in the original adaptation of Stephen King’s It, has died. He was 80 years old.
body: TMZ was first to report Curry's death. The actor reportedly died Tuesday at his Los Angeles home. Curry suffered a major stroke in 2012 that affected his mobility and memory, though he continued to perform in voice roles and in special appearances. He voiced Chancellor Palpatine/Darth Sidious in the animated series Star Wars: The Clone Wars.

Curry's acting career started on the stage. He originally portrayed Dr. Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Show in London and on Broadway. He reprised the role in the 1975 film version of that musical, The Rocky Horror Picture Show, which was a modest success at release but went on to be an enduring cult hit, ultimately grossing more than $170 million at the box office.

In the 1980s, Curry achieved mainstream stardom in films such as the musical Annie, Ridley Scott's fantasy film Legend, and the board game adaptation whodunnit Clue. Later, Curry starred in memorable roles in The Hunt for Red October, the superhero film The Shadow, Muppet Treasure Island, and Congo.

articles.title: A Legendary Star Wars Vending Machine Is At The Center Of A Major Conspiracy
articles.summary: More than 27 years ago, Star Wars: Episode 1 - The Phantom Menace released in theaters, ushering in a new wave of fandom for one of the most important media franchises of all time. Since the film's release, one relic has been a constant: the Pepsi vending machine on Mt. Washington in Pittsburgh.
body: Below, you can see what the vending machine looks like--or looked like, depending on its fate. The graphics have faded over time but it's still drawing in thirsty customers with its giant Pepsi bottle on the front alongside some pod-racing action.
This week, however, the machine went missing. It was replaced with a pretty hilarious decoy, featuring a very poorly drawn recreation of the original machine's artwork.

Visitors have noticed that the new machine has 10 buttons, while the original only had nine. It's been speculated that influencer Braeden Days may have swiped it, as he has threatened to do so in the past. It's possible the locals or the Pittsburgh Fire Department had something to do with it, as well, as it's located just outside a fire station.
The new artwork has been compared to the infamous 2012 Jesus-painting restoration, though it will be a lot easier to laugh at if the original machine makes a return.

articles.title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy Feels More Like a Tomb Raider Game
articles.summary: There is nary a single rat in Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy, a new installment that acts as a prequel to the 14th-century series. While it carries the Plague Tale name, so much of the design ethos that makes up the experience bears little resemblance to anything in either Innocence or Requiem.
body: If you were to ask the average gamer what they knew about the Plague Tale series, you'd probably get a one-word answer: rats. Asobo Studio successfully carved out a niche with its Plague Tale duology, consisting of 2019's Innocence and 2022's Requiem, by rooting the series in a compelling set of design pillars. They featured stealth-focused combat, contained emotional storytelling, and — most importantly — gave you the ability to control writhing hordes of murderous rats. With the latest entry in the series, Asobo asks how many of those core pillars it can throw out while still feeling like a Plague Tale game.

articles.title: PlayStation Plus September 2026 Free Games Lineup Officially Revealed, Includes a Great Retro RPG
articles.summary: On Wednesday, Sony revealed the next batch of PlayStation Plus subscribers' free Essential games. Like most months, there's a little something for everyone on offer: Chained Echoes, Sniper Elite: Resistance, Wobbly Life, and MLB The Show 26 make up September 2026's offerings.
body: Chained Echoes is a 16-bit turn-based RPG from 2022. Its world is full of fantastical creatures and magic, but also giant mechs. Basically, if you ever wanted to see a Gundam fight a dragon, give Chained Echoes a spin. Developer Umami Tiger (Matthias Linda) describes it as "a story-driven JRPG where a group of heroes travel around the vast continent of Valandis to bring an end to the war between its three kingdoms." Like so many RPGs, there's some heft to Chained Echoes as it'll take you 30-40 hours to complete. Every enemy will be visible, so at least there won't be any random encounters making the experience feel bloated.

articles.title: Xbox’s Disc-To-Digital Program Officially Revealed, Launches Next Week
articles.summary: Xbox has officially revealed a new disc-to-digital program that will allow players to add physical copies of their games to a digital library. The program, which was first reported to be in the works this July, is launching in a matter of days on Aug. 31.
body: Jason Ronald, Xbox VP Next Generation, made the announcement today in an Xbox Wire post. "Today we are introducing a feature that brings the benefits of digital to physical discs, giving players more flexibility in how they access and play supported games across the Xbox ecosystem," said Ronald. "This is part of our broader commitment to game preservation. As technology, devices, and distribution continue to evolve, preserving access to the games people own matters more than ever." Players enrolled in the Xbox Insider program will be able to test the feature starting next week.

articles.title: Fool's Theory explains where The Witcher 3's expansion region Letten actually is, and it's close to the setting of The Witcher 4
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red properly revealed new Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past yesterday during Opening Night Live, confirming the new playable location as Letten, the place Geralt's best friend bard pal Dandelion comes from. But where exactly is Letten on the map? It's bloody hard to find.
body: Indeed, I'm not sure it's marked at all on any maps yet because it's a location CDPR has padded out to set this original Witcher story in. But we do finally have official guidance on how to find it. That guidance comes from Peter Gelencser, who's the world director of Songs of the Past at developer Fool's Theory - the co-developer of the expansion.

Gelencser was speaking in a CDPR Gamescom stream earlier today and clarified: "The whole thing plays out in Letten, which is the birthplace of Dandelion. It's in the north, somewhere half-way between Kovir [I think he says Kovir] and Kaedwen for all you map nerds out there. If you go to the Gulf of Praxeda and take the Buina river to the east and take a right on the Nimnar river, on the other southern shore of the Nimnar you will find this lovely place.
"But it's in the north if you want the TLDR version," Gelencser said.

articles.title: Hugely anticipated anime RPG Ananta gets a January release date, as pre-registrations hit a whopping 17m sign-ups
articles.summary: Ananta, the free-to-play open-world game that looks a whole lot like Grand Theft Auto's urban sandbox got an anime makeover, finally has a release date.
body: Publisher NetEase and China-based developer Naked Rain announced that Ananta is launching worldwide on 15th January, 2027 for PC, PlayStation 5 and mobile devices, years after it first debuted under the working title of Project Mugen.

A snazzy new trailer also debuted at last night's Gamescom Opening Night Live show, showing off some giant skylines and, well, a bit of everything, really - open-world driving, cycling, skateboarding, flying, stealth, melee combat, in-game social media apps, a seemingly massive cast of characters, and an even more massive UFO that comes out of nowhere. I did say everything, after all. Take a look.

While punching up thugs and getting into car chases are a big part of the trailer above, Ananta's promising that the full game will be much more focused on becoming an influencer in pursuit of endless attention. NetEase says there's a unique social media platform in the game, and you can take steps to grow your follower list over time, presumably by punching up thugs and livestreaming a UFO invasion, that is. A few Gamescoms ago, we saw a toilet with legs running about, which should also be good algorithm fodder when the time comes.

Dune: Awakening is launching September 22 for PlayStation 5 (PS5) and Xbox Series X|S, and Xbox Cloud, with the game being available now on PC (Xbox on PC, Steam).
